# CG-RES-018: Success response added

A new success (2XX) response was added.

**Why it matters:** Many consumers treat any 2xx as success, but some branch on exact codes.

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Area | [Responses](./#res) |
| Detects | `response.added` |
| Severity | breaking: high · potentially breaking: medium · undetermined: medium |
| Classification can be overridden | no (the rule only fires when the change is breaking by definition) |

## Message

> New success response {status} for {operation}.
>
> Consumers that only handle the previous success statuses may not handle {status}.
>
> **Fix:** Make sure consumers treat any 2xx as success.

## Examples

Each example is an executed test case of the rule (`packages/engine/test/compat/fixtures.ts`).

### Fires: 202 added beside 200

```diff
  openapi: 3.1.0
  info: {title: t, version: v}
  paths:
    /x:
      get:
-       responses: {'200': {description: ok}}
+       responses: {'200': {description: ok}, '202': {description: accepted}}
```

**Result:** Potentially breaking, medium. New success response 202 for GET /x.

### Does not fire: error response added

```diff
  openapi: 3.1.0
  info: {title: t, version: v}
  paths:
    /x:
      get:
-       responses: {'200': {description: ok}}
+       responses: {'200': {description: ok}, '400': {description: bad}}
```

**Result:** no finding from this rule.

## Limitations

- Consumers often treat any 2xx as success.

## Silence or tune it

```yaml
rules:
  ignore:
    - rule: CG-RES-018
      operation: "GET /example"   # optional: narrow it down
      reason: "Explain why this is acceptable"
      expires: 2027-01-01         # optional
  overrides:
    CG-RES-018: { severity: low }
```
